Learning Outcomes

Identify the layers of the heart and their tissues:
    Epicardium
    Myocardium
    Endocardium
Identify Purkinje fibers in the ventricles as part of the cardiac conduction system
Distinguish between the epicardium and endocardium
Distinguish between regular cardiac muscle fibers and Purkinje fibers (modified cardiac muscle fibers)

                                                            Endocardium: 3 layers / 3 tissue types
                                                             Layer 1 = Epithelial layer: Endothelium: simple squamous epithelium (tissue 1)
                                                             Layer 2 = Subendothelial connective tissue layer: areolar connective tissue (tissue 2)
                                                             Layer 3 = Subendocardial layer: deep connective tissue containing Purkinje fibers (tissues 2–3)
                                                A Flat nuclei of endothelial cells
                                                    B Subendothelial areolar connective tissue
                                                C Subendocardial connective tissue surrounding Purkinje fibers (not clearly visible)
                                                D Purkinje fibers — modified cardiac muscle fibers (cross section) (tissue 3)

Slide 4: Comparison of Purkinje fibers of the Conduction System and Regular cardiac muscle tissue



                                                  Purkinje fibers in Subendocardium — modified cardiac muscle tissue (cross section)
                                                 ID: Large, round to polygonal modified cardiac muscle cells of variable sizes
                                                            central nuclei, abundant pale-staining glycogen in cytoplasm
                                               few pink-staining peripheral myofibrils, resulting in minimal striations





                                       Myocardium — regular cardiac muscle tissue (cross section)
                                             ID: Small, round to polygonal cardiac muscle cells of variable sizes
                                                              •  central nuclei, pale glycogen around the nucleus
                                                              •  abundant pink-staining myofibrils in cross-section, resulting in no visible striations





Both: round to polygonal cells of variable sizes → central nuclei → pink-staining myofibrils
Regular cardiac muscle: small → pale glycogen around nucleus → abundant myofibrils → no visible striations
Purkinje fibers: large → abundant pale glycogen → few peripheral myofibrils → minimal striations

Comparison of Epicardium and Endocardium

                                     The endocardium has an additional deep subendocardial layer, which has no equivalent in the epicardium

     o   Epicardium

2.   Regular cardiac muscle tissue
     o   Regular cardiac muscle fibers (longitudinal and cross sections)
     o   Central nucleus
     o   Branching fibers
     o   Cross-striations
     o   Intercalated discs
     o   Endomysial connective tissue
     o   Fibroblast nucleus
     o   Capillary and Red blood cells
     o   Endothelial cell nucleus
     o   Collagen fibers
3.   Epicardium
     o   Mesothelium
     o   Subepicardial (submesothelial) connective tissues: fibroblast and collagen
          o   areolar and adipose tissues
     o   Coronary vessels
     o   Peripheral nerve
4.   Endocardium / conduction system
     o   Endothelium
     o   Subendothelial connective tissue: fibroblast and collagen
     o   Subendocardial layer, containing Purkinje fibers
     o   Regular cardiac muscle fibers for comparison with Purkinje fibers (modified cardiac muscle fibers)
